source_text: A 2022 modeling analysis across 13 countries found VMMC cost-effective (defined as less than three times the gross domestic product per capita per disability-adjusted life year averted) in 62% of scenarios with adult HIV incidence exceeding 1.5 per 100 person-years, with effectiveness increasing in higher-incidence areas due to greater absolute risk reduction.00515-0/fulltext) The World Health Organization's 2023 review of programmatic data from priority countries affirmed VMMC as highly cost-effective or cost-saving in nearly all evaluated scenarios, attributing this to low per-procedure costs (typically $50–150) and the intervention's one-time nature, which averts lifelong treatment expenses estimated at $1,000–2,000 annually per person on antiretrovirals. [57]
